# Template: projectile_motion
A projectile's parabolic trajectory computed from real kinematics (g = 10 unless set): launched at a given speed and angle, from the ground or from a platform of some height, the path is sampled from the exact closed-form y(x), with velocity-vector arrows at launch, apex (horizontal only — vertical velocity is zero at the top) and landing, optional dashed horizontal/vertical component arrows, a hatched ground line, and with show_values the angle, v₀, range R and apex height H written on the figure. speed, angle_deg and height are plain numeric params, so an `animate` can sweep any of them and the parabola, apex and vectors re-derive themselves frame by frame. The scale is set by the SPEED (a 45° launch at this speed fills the width), not by the angle: a swept angle shows the real range and height change — 45° lands farthest on level ground, and two angles adding to 90° land together. `view` fixes the scale outright (for a speed sweep). Choose this scene for ANY request about projectile motion, trajectory, range, a launch angle, time of flight, or the height/velocity of a thrown or fired object (ignoring air resistance). Paused, the viewer drags the tip of the v₀ arrow (angle and speed), the platform (launch height), and with show_values scrubs or taps the angle and v₀ numbers; the previous flight stays as a faint ghost, and every value recomputes live ({projectile.range}, max_height, time, angle, v0).
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "speed": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "Launch speed, 1-10 arbitrary units (default 6). Animatable."
  },
  "angle_deg": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "Launch angle above the horizontal, 5-85 degrees (default 45). Animatable."
  },
  "height": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "Launch height above the ground, 0-10 units (default 0): a platform is drawn under the launch point. Animatable."
  },
  "gravity": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "g, 1-30 units (default 10)."
  },
  "show_vectors": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Velocity arrows at launch, apex and landing (default true)."
  },
  "show_components": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Dashed horizontal/vertical component arrows at launch and landing, when show_vectors is also true (default false)."
  },
  "label_apex": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Label the apex point (default true); with show_values it reads its height, H = …"
  },
  "show_values": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Write the numbers on the figure: the launch angle (an arc and 45°), v₀ = 6 on the launch arrow, the range R under the ground, the apex height H (default false). The viewer can scrub or tap the angle and v₀."
  },
  "ghost": {
   "type": "object",
   "description": "An earlier flight drawn faint and dashed to compare with, e.g. {speed: 6, angle_deg: 30}. The live drag sets it to the flight before the drag.",
   "properties": {
    "speed": {
     "type": "number"
    },
    "angle_deg": {
     "type": "number"
    },
    "height": {
     "type": "number"
    }
   }
  },
  "view": {
   "type": "object",
   "description": "Fix the scale: the range across and the height up the page holds, e.g. {range: 5, height: 3.3}. A flight too big for it still fits: the page pulls back. The live drag sets it.",
   "properties": {
    "range": {
     "type": "number"
    },
    "height": {
     "type": "number"
    }
   },
   "required": [
    "range",
    "height"
   ]
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- ground: the ground line and hatching (one group)
- platform: the block the projectile is launched from, present when height > 0
- path: the trajectory parabola
- ghost_path: the earlier flight, faint and dashed, present when ghost is set
- v0 / v_apex / v_land: the velocity-vector arrows at launch, apex (horizontal only) and landing, present when show_vectors
- vx_<k> / vy_<k>: dashed horizontal/vertical component arrows (k=0 launch, k=1 landing), present when show_vectors and show_components
- apex_label: the "Apex" caption ("H = 1.8" with show_values), present when label_apex
- angle_arc / angle_value: the launch-angle arc and its "45°" (show_values)
- speed_value: the "v₀ = 6" beside the launch arrow (show_values with show_vectors; it replaces the arrow's own v₀ label)
- range_mark: the range dimension under the ground with its "R = 3.6" (show_values)
- height_mark: the dashed drop from the apex to the ground (show_values)
Examples:
Request: "Show projectile motion at 45 degrees." → params: {"speed":6,"angle_deg":45}
Request: "Show the horizontal and vertical velocity components of a projectile launched at a steep angle." → params: {"speed":8,"angle_deg":70,"show_components":true}
Request: "Compare a 30 degree throw with a 60 degree throw." → params: {"speed":8,"angle_deg":60,"show_values":true,"ghost":{"angle_deg":30}}
Request: "Why does a shot put fly farthest below 45 degrees?" → params: {"speed":8,"angle_deg":45,"height":2,"show_values":true}

Viewer can: Drag the v0 arrow's tip (angle and speed) or the platform (launch height); the path, apex and readouts follow, the last throw stays as a ghost.

In YAML: `template: projectile_motion` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
